title: The Bad Air
text: The candles gutter, shrink and burn blue. Your breath comes short; your heartbeat is loud in your ears. The air down here is thin and wrong, tasting of old pennies. The dead rats along the wall all died facing the way you came.

options.label: Hold your breath and hurry through, before the air takes hold of you.

outcomes.text: Lungs burning, vision greying at the edges, everyone makes it through by the barest margin.
Someone breathes. The air gets inside their head and rearranges things, leaving them out of place.

options.label: The sharpest nose follows a faint draught, hoping it leads to clean air.

outcomes.text: The draught leads to a side passage of clean air. Someone hid something there long ago, against a day like this.

options.label: Turn back and find another way. Whatever killed those rats is still in the air.

outcomes.text: The other way is longer. The taste of old pennies stays in your mouths the whole way.
